preferences: A Thai-style dip for food cooked in plain water: fresh lime acidity, balanced salty umami, a little sweetness, and garlic and herbal aromas. Chili heat is welcome; the diner can eat spicy food. Choose heat, richness, and aromatics that work together without overpowering the food.

A non-spicy Thai-style dip for food cooked in plain water, with balanced acidity and salty umami, a little sweetness, and gentle garlic and sesame aromas. No chili heat or Sichuan-pepper tingling or numbness. Avoid chili-containing condiments, even mildly spicy sweet chili sauce, and keep the dip balanced.

A Thai-style sour, salty, moderately spicy dip for food cooked in plain water. Do not add leafy herbs or green vegetable garnishes: no cilantro (including the station condiment labelled Parsley) or scallions (labelled Minced shallots). In this experiment, no vegetables means no cilantro or scallion pieces; garlic, chili, mushrooms, and prepared sauces remain allowed. Balance umami, acidity, a little sweetness, and garlic aroma.
